extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer-algebra system (mathematicians / computational algebraists) who use the sheafcoh.lib library to compute sheaf cohomology and truncated graded modules.
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for procedures in the SINGULAR sheafcoh.lib library (e.g., truncate, truncateFast) giving usage signatures, input assumptions, return values, and example behaviour for computing truncated modules/sheaf cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: truncate(M,d) — usage and input type
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: truncate(M,d); M module, d int. Assume: M is graded, and it comes assigned with an admissible degree vector as an attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input must be a graded module M with an admissible degree vector attribute. Example usage: LIB "sheafcoh.lib"; ring R=0,(x,y,z),dp; module M=maxideal(3); homog(M); module M2=truncate(M,2);

rubrics_metrics.name: truncate(M,d) — return and meaning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is a presentation matrix for the truncation of coker(M) at degree d. Example checks in the docs show printing M2 and using dimGradedPart(M2,k) to inspect graded pieces (e.g., dimGradedPart(M2,2) matches dimGradedPart(M,2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: truncateFast(M,d) — usage and input assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: truncateFast(M,d); M module, d int. Assume: M is graded, and it comes assigned with an admissible degree vector as an attribute 'isHomog'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: truncateFast is a fast + experimental version. The docs state: 'Fast + experimental version. M shoud be a SB!' (i.e., M should be given as a standard basis). In examples the call is often used as truncateFast(std(M),d) to ensure a standard basis before calling.

rubrics_metrics.name: truncateFast — printlevel / verbosity controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavior depending on printlevel: if printlevel>=1, step-by-step timings printed; if >=2, progress debug messages printed; if >=3, all intermediate results printed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use printlevel to control verbosity during truncateFast execution for diagnostics/timing. Examples in the docs show timing comparisons between truncate and truncateFast and printing timing outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement / guidance: ensure grading attribute ('isHomog') to shift grading
rubrics_metrics.description: You can shift the grading of M by assigning attrib(M,'isHomog',v) (e.g., intvec v=1; attrib(M,'isHomog',v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examples show that after changing the 'isHomog' attribute and re-running truncate/truncateFast, the printed presentation and dimGradedPart results change accordingly. Use this to adapt/troubleshoot graded-degree behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation / equality checks after truncation
rubrics_metrics.description: The docs demonstrate validating outputs by comparing results of truncate vs truncateFast (e.g., checking NF(M2, std(M2t)) + size(NF(M2t, std(M2))) etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: time both methods, compute M2t=truncate(M,2) and M2=truncateFast(std(M),2), then check equivalence/normal forms and compare dimGradedPart values (e.g., dimGradedPart(M2,2) == dimGradedPart(M,2)). Use std(M) and NF/size checks as in examples to confirm equivalence.
